key_insight: In long axisymmetric channels with thin electric double layers, diffusioosmotic flow is governed by channel geometry, while imposed pressure adds only an extra hydraulic contribution and does not change the diffusioosmotic component.
engineering_relevance: This provides a design rule for micro- and nanofluidic channels to tune flow rate and ionic transport by shaping the channel, including a practical cylinder approximation for estimating resistance.
method: Theory for coupled salt concentration and pressure-driven flow in axisymmetric channels
Derivation of flow-rate relations separating diffusioosmotic and pressure-driven contributions
Comparison across several channel geometries to assess how shape alters flow and ionic flux
evidence_signal: The paper reports calculated p(Q) curves for several axisymmetric channels and finds they are nearly linear, with slopes that depend sensitively on shape.
watch_item: The theory assumes thin diffuse layers and long channels, so performance may deviate for short channels, strong overlap of double layers, or strongly non-ideal geometries.
paper_title: Diffusioosmosis of electrolyte solutions in axisymmetric channels
